text:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
characteristic_form: The agent calls wo.list_workorders (site_id=MAIN, asset_num=Transformer 1, status=APPROVED_PENDING, page_size=0) and wo.get_workorder for details. It also calls wo.list_workorders with status=OPEN to find duplicates. It retrieves the latest DGA values with iot.latest_reading and classifies the fault with fmsr.interpret_dga, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene for the IEC 60599 class and co for paper involvement. Each pending work order has one of three outcomes: approved with wo.approve_workorder, cancelled as a newer duplicate with wo.cancel_workorder and the older WO number in the reason, or left pending with a justification. For approved arcing, discharge or OLTC work orders, priority is set to 1 with wo.update_workorder only if acetylene exceeds 1 ppm. Fallback when any of the five fault gases is null: only routine sampling WOs are approved, only exact duplicates are cancelled, and the missing gas is named. Fallback when no pending WOs exist: the agent says so and advises whether the DGA condition justifies a new WO. The output is a per-WO outcome table with its supporting evidence.

text:
I'm worried that urgent work on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is stuck behind an overloaded technician. Give me the MAIN site's work order KPIs for the last 6 months, including backlog, overdue count and average completion time. Then list every open work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority, scheduled date and assigned technician, and flag which ones are overdue.

For each technician assigned to those work orders, count how many open work orders they currently hold at MAIN. Anyone holding more than 5 counts as overloaded.

Next, work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630.

If Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, do the following for any overdue work order on it that sits with an overloaded technician. Reassign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among those who have worked on Transformer 1 before and are not overloaded. Give it a start date within the next 7 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If it is Condition 1, don't reassign anything. Just list the overdue items and recommend a catch-up order, ranked by priority and then by how late they are.

If every technician with Transformer 1 history is overloaded, don't reassign. Tell me who is least loaded and recommend bringing in outside help. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
characteristic_form: The agent calls wo.get_workorder_kpis (site_id=MAIN, period_months=6) for backlog, overdue and completion metrics. It calls wo.list_workorders (asset_num=Transformer 1, status=OPEN) and wo.get_workorder to get assignees and scheduled dates, then flags overdue items. It counts each technician's open load with wo.get_my_assigned_workorders (open_only=true, site_id=MAIN) and marks anyone with more than 5 as overloaded. It identifies technicians with Transformer 1 history from closed WOs via wo.list_workorders. It computes TDCG from iot.latest_reading using the six combustible gases, carrying forward nulls from iot.history with a flag, and maps the total to the IEEE C57.104 condition. At Condition 2 or higher, overdue WOs held by overloaded technicians are reassigned with wo.assign_technician to the least-loaded, non-overloaded technician with Transformer 1 history. The new start date is within 7 days, chosen from wo.get_schedule_calendar to avoid days with 3 or more scheduled WOs. At Condition 1, the agent only lists overdue items and gives a catch-up ranking by priority and then lateness. Fallback: if every qualified technician is overloaded, no reassignment is made, and the agent names the least-loaded technician and recommends outside help.
